title: Dedicated: autoscaling burst controls, throughput guarantees, and utilization reporting
author: Nora Jackson
release_notes: Added burst token bucket controls and SLA-facing throughput guarantees for Dedicated; new utilization reporting endpoints and dashboards. No breaking changes to public API. Operators must enable new feature flags when upgrading.
description: Context and motivation: Customers using Dedicated have reported bursts of traffic that either overrun pool capacity (causing queuing and tail latency) or idle capacity that is not available for short-term bursts because autoscaler reacts too slowly. This PR implements a conservative, operator-configurable 'burst token bucket' overlay on top of existing autoscaling policies, introduces explicit throughput guarantees (SLO config) per capacity pool, and adds utilization reporting and per-pool metrics to help tune policies. Summary of changes (high-level commits): - Add burst controller and token-bucket overlay (nora/burst-controller) - Wire burst constraints into scheduler and capacity allocator (nora/scheduler-integration) - Add throughput_guarantee to pool config and admission checks (nora/pool-config) - Export new metrics (dedicated.pool.{utilization,burst_tokens,guaranteed_throughput}) and Prometheus scrape targets (nora/metrics) - Add REST endpoints and Console hooks for pool-level utilization and history (nora/console-api) - Unit + integration tests and updated docs (nora/tests-docs) Changed areas/files (high level): - src/dedicated/autoscaler/burst_controller.rs: new token bucket implementation and config parsing - src/dedicated/scheduler/mod.rs: admission checks now consult burst controller and throughput guarantees - src/dedicated/pool/config.rs: added throughput_guarantee, burst_capacity fields to PoolConfig, with migration logic - src/console/api/pool_metrics.go: endpoints for historical utilization and burst usage - infra/helm/dedicated/values.yaml: feature flag and default params - docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md: operator guide and recommended tuning - tests/integration/dedicated_burst_test.py: end-to-end scenario tests - prometheus/rules/dedicated_alerts.yaml: new alert on sustained saturation Review conversation (condensed): - Diego Ramos (reviewer): "Good direction. Two requests: 1) make burst defaults opt-in behind a feature flag and document upgrade steps; 2) add a safety cap so bursts can't starve reserved acks." - Nora Jackson (author): "Both addressed — defaults are behind feature flag (infra/helm/values.yaml), and scheduler now enforces reserved_tokens floor before honoring burst tokens. Added tests." - Maya Chen (reviewer): "Please add a small benchmark showing latency impact under normal load and during bursts." - Nora Jackson: "Added perf micro-benchmarks in perf-canary/bench/ and included summary in docs. Impact on p50/p95 under normal load is negligible; p99 during aggressive bursts shows 8-15% increase unless guarantee is configured." - Ava Patel (approver): "Approvals after nits fixed." CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests (flaky on first run): 1 failure on ded. allocation test due to race; reran -> pass - Lint: pass - Performance canary (subset): pass with build tag perf-sim The PR was marked as ready for final review after addressing comments. Merge outcome: merged via squash (squash commit message includes linked Linear tasks and short changelog). Notes for operators and upgrade: - Burst behavior is off by default; enable with helm value dedicated.enableBurstController=true and tune dedicated.burst.* parameters. - When enabling for the first time, operators should set conservative burst_window_seconds and burst_capacity to avoid rapid scaling churn. - Throughput guarantees require configuring pool.guaranteed_throughput_rps; requests that would exceed the guarantee are admitted into best-effort queue or routed to fallback pools depending on policy. Observability and rollout guidance: - New metrics to monitor: dedicated_pool_utilization, dedicated_pool_burst_tokens, dedicated_pool_guaranteed_throughput. Dashboards added under Console -> Dedicated -> Pool Metrics. - Recommend canary rollout: enable feature flag in a single region / small pool size, monitor p99 and burst token depletion, then expand. Related tickets and follow-ups: - ENG-7128: refine autoscaler heuristics to prefer warm instances for bursts - ENG-7131: add per-customer pool prioritization in future iteration - SUP-842: customer report that motivated throughput guarantees This PR touches operator-visible configs and adds metrics — no breaking changes to client-facing APIs. If issues observed after rollout, revert by disabling dedicated.enableBurstController and restoring previous pool configs.
